newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's real drops 0.15 pct on lower mini-band.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's real drops 0.15 pct on lower mini-band.

text.p: Brazil's real fell 0.15 percent to close at 1.0236 against the dollar in calm trading after the Central Bank set a weaker level for the currency, dealers said.
In the morning the Central Bank set a new mini-band for the real between 1.0235 and 1.0285 reais per greenback, a drop of 0.15 percent, which surprised the market.
Analysts said the market expected the central bank to lower the mini-band by no more than 0.10 percent.
Traders said the Central Bank move was designed to end uncertainties in the foreign exchange market and avoid delays in export contracts.
Preliminary figures for commercial and financial foreign exchange contracts showed a Wednesday surplus of $176 million.
In the interbank forex floating rate market, the real closed at 1.0293 to the dollar, up 0.14 percent.
In the illegal parallel market, the real closed steady at 1.040 per greenback, traders said.
